beats.say: A penny gets you a whole record collection. And you never see the bill.
Sign up for a penny and get twelve records promised.
Or pick the regular club plan with a set monthly fee and no upfront lure.
Or choose the premium package that bundles extra merch for a higher price.
Members who ignored the deadline got a full-price album shipped. Looks like a mistake.
But it does a job - the penny is a hook, the real cost hides later.
The contract required you to buy a minimum number of albums, so the next shipment arrived with a full-price bill.
That hidden purchase drove revenue to $1.4 billion in 1996 before collapsing to $17 million by 2014.
You see it everywhere: a gym offers a free week, then forces a $30 class fee each week.
A coffee shop sells a $1 pastry, then auto-adds a $5 latte each visit.
A streaming app lures with $0.99 for month one, then locks you into $12 monthly.
Watch for a tiny upfront cost that unlocks an automatic larger charge. Follow for more.
